claim.claim: Walmart's operating income for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 was higher than in the same quarter a year earlier.

verdict.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: operating income increased $1.4 billion and $1.6 billion for the three and six months ended July 31, 2026, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year.

Three Months Ended July 31, Six Months Ended July 31, (Amounts in millions) 2026 2025 2026 2025 Net sales $ 186,100 $ 175,750 $ 361,784 $ 339,731 Percentage change from comparable period 5.9 % 4.8 % 6.5 % 3.7 % Operating income $ 9,383 $ 7,286 $ 16,876 $ 14,421 Percentage change from comparable period 28.8 % (8.2) % 17.0 % (2.4) %

verdict.reasoning_summary: The claim states that Walmart's operating income for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 was higher than in the same quarter a year earlier. Evidence E5 provides a clear table showing operating income for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was $9,383 million compared to $7,286 million for the three months ended July 31, 2025, representing a 28.8% increase. Evidence E1 confirms this by stating that "operating income increased $1.4 billion...for the three...months ended July 31, 2026...when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year." The difference of $9,383M - $7,286M = $2,097M is approximately $2.1 billion (note: there's a slight discrepancy with the $1.4B stated in E1, but both sources confirm an increase). The claim is fully supported by the evidence.
